headline: High-risk shared filesystem and shell overlap create prompt-injection, leakage, and conflict hazards; Cursor’s Yolo mode and broad egress amplify the pair.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor ingests workspace files and clipboard contents, and the course agent also reads/writes files in a local development environment. That shared filesystem bridge lets attacker-controlled content from either side be treated as instructions. No direct provenance or isolation is documented for the pair, so the interaction is inferred from both profiles.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace directory or copied clipboard text
IF either agent parses file contents as instructions or tool directives
mitigations: Separate the agents into different workspaces
Disable clipboard-based handoff between agents
Require explicit human review of any file-derived instructions
Use read-only mounts for shared inputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for inter-agent content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents read files and handle secrets; Cursor also has broad network egress and calls external model providers, while the course agent exposes configuration secrets and API endpoints. In a shared workspace, sensitive files can flow into either agent’s outputs or upstream APIs. The pairwise leakage path is plausible but not directly documented, so uncertainty stays elevated.
conditions: IF sensitive files or .env material are present in the shared workspace
IF either agent forwards file contents to a third-party model or API
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared directories
Rotate any exposed API keys before use
Restrict outbound network access for one agent
Review logs for file-content uploads
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent secret isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can execute shell commands and write the filesystem; Cursor can also modify git state, while the course agent runs local development workflows with Docker Compose. On a shared directory, concurrent writes and git mutations can corrupt state or overwrite each other. The overlap is explicit in both profiles and dangerous by default if co-located.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or working tree
IF Cursor Yolo mode auto-runs commands while the course agent is also mutating files
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Pause one agent before the other writes
Disable Yolo mode during shared edits
Use git branches per agent
requires-engineering: add file-locking or orchestration locks

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor’s agent loop can generate code or edits that the course agent may consume in notebooks, scripts, or API workflows. The course agent’s LangGraph pipeline can then act on those outputs without a documented verification gate. Because the pair lacks explicit cross-agent validation, errors can cascade from one agent’s output into the other’s actions.
conditions: IF outputs from Cursor are copied into the course agent’s prompts or notebooks
IF the course agent executes generated code or instructions without review
mitigations: Require a human check before reuse of generated artifacts
Add a verification step between agents
Limit the course agent to read-only analysis of Cursor output
Keep generated code in a staging folder
requires-engineering: add schema validation for inter-agent handoffs

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor handles source code, open files, and clipboard contents, while the course agent touches academic papers, metadata, and configuration secrets. If regulated or confidential material is placed in the shared environment, the pair can create retention and residency mismatches through local files and external API calls. The profiles do not document a specific regulatory regime, so this is a general compliance risk rather than a proven violation.
conditions: IF regulated data or customer secrets are stored in the shared workspace
IF external API calls process that data without a matching retention policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair’s workspace
Review vendor retention settings before use
Separate secret-bearing projects from research notebooks
Document data-handling rules for both agents
requires-engineering: perform a formal compliance review
